hindi: जड़, छाल, सार, निर्यास, नाल, स्वरस, कोमल पत्ते, क्षार, क्षीर, फल, फूल, भस्म, तेल, काँटे,
english: Root, bark, heartwood, exudate, stalk, expressed juice, tender leaves, alkalis, milky latex, fruit, flower, ash, oils, thorns,
notes: The list of plant parts used as drugs continues into 74a, where it is summed up as the plant (audbhida) group. kṣīra here is the milky sap of plants, not animal milk (context of plant products).
lines_deva: क्षाराः क्षीरं फलं पुष्पं भस्म तैलानि कण्टकाः
lines_iast: kṣārāḥ kṣīraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ bhasma tailāni kaṇṭakāḥ

hindi: पत्ते, कोंपलें, कन्द और अंकुर — यह औद्भिद गण है। मूलिनी सोलह और फलिनी उन्नीस कही गई हैं।
english: leaves, leaf-buds, bulbs and shoots: this is the plant (audbhida) group. The root-drugs (mūlinī) are declared to be sixteen and the fruit-drugs (phalinī) nineteen.
notes: ekonā goes with viṃśatiḥ: "twenty less one" = nineteen (confirmed by 86a phalāny ekonaviṃśatiḥ). mūlinī = plants whose root is the useful part; phalinī = plants whose fruit is used.

hindi: चार महास्नेह और पाँच ही लवण हैं; आठ मूत्र गिनाए गए हैं और आठ ही दूध।
english: There are four great fats (mahāsneha) and just five salts; eight urines are enumerated, and likewise eight milks.

words.gram: ppp. m. nom. pl. ni-√dṛś caus.

hindi: और शोधन के लिए छह वृक्ष पुनर्वसु ने बताए हैं। जो इन्हें रोगों में प्रयोग करना जानता है, वह वेद का ज्ञाता है।
english: And six trees for purification (śodhana) have been pointed out by Punarvasu. He who knows how to apply these in disorders is a knower of the Veda.
notes: Punarvasu: name of the teacher (Punarvasu Ātreya in this text). vedavit: literally "knower of the Veda"; it may mean the knower of this science (Āyurveda) rather than of the Vedas generally. The six trees are not named in this chunk.
lines_deva: य एतान् वेत्ति संयोक्तुं विकारेषु स वेदवित्
lines_iast: ya etān vetti saṃyoktuṃ vikāreṣu sa vedavit

hindi: हस्तिदन्ती, हैमवती, श्यामा, त्रिवृत्, अधोगुडा, सप्तला, श्वेता नाम वाली, प्रत्यक्श्रेणी और गवाक्षी भी,
english: Hastidantī, haimavatī, śyāmā, trivṛt, adhoguḍā, saptalā, the one named śvetā, pratyakśreṇī and also gavākṣī,
notes: List of the sixteen root-drugs (mūlinī), continued in 78. Identifications: trivṛt = Operculina turpethum, Hindi निशोथ (standard); śyāmā = the dark variety of trivṛt (probable); hastidantī = a large dantī, Baliospermum montanum or allied (disputed); pratyakśreṇī = dantī, Baliospermum montanum, Hindi दन्ती (probable); haimavatī = disputed (white vacā or Iris species proposed); adhoguḍā = disputed (Argyreia nervosa, vṛddhadāruka, proposed); saptalā = disputed (an Acacia or Euphorbia species proposed); śvetā = disputed (white-flowered Clitoria ternatea, Hindi अपराजिता, often proposed); gavākṣī = disputed (a colocynth-like cucurbit, indravāruṇī type, proposed).

hindi: ज्योतिष्मती, बिम्बी, शणपुष्पी, विषाणिका, अजगन्धा, द्रवन्ती और यहाँ सोलहवीं क्षीरिणी है।
english: jyotiṣmatī, bimbī, śaṇapuṣpī, viṣāṇikā, ajagandhā, dravantī, and kṣīriṇī, the sixteenth here.
notes: Identifications: jyotiṣmatī = Celastrus paniculatus, Hindi मालकांगनी (standard); bimbī = Coccinia grandis, Hindi कुंदरू (standard); śaṇapuṣpī = Crotalaria verrucosa or allied, Hindi झुनझुनिया (probable); ajagandhā = Cleome gynandra or Gynandropsis, Hindi हुरहुर (probable); viṣāṇikā = disputed (Helicteres isora and others proposed); dravantī = disputed (a Croton or Jatropha species proposed); kṣīriṇī = disputed (a latex-bearing plant; several candidates). Count 77+78 = 16, matching 74b.
lines_deva: ज्योतिष्मती च बिम्बी च शणपुष्पी विषाणिका
अजगन्धा द्रवन्ती च क्षीरिणी चात्र षोडशी
lines_iast: jyotiṣmatī ca bimbī ca śaṇapuṣpī viṣāṇikā
ajagandhā dravantī ca kṣīriṇī cātra ṣoḍaśī

hindi: शणपुष्पी, बिम्बी और हैमवती भी वमन में, तथा श्वेता और ज्योतिष्मती शिरोविरेचन में प्रयोग करनी चाहिए।
english: Śaṇapuṣpī, bimbī and also haimavatī are to be used in emesis (vamana), and śvetā and jyotiṣmatī in head-evacuation (śīrṣavirecana, errhine therapy).
notes: "ca cchardane": the doubled cch is regular sandhi after a short vowel (ca + chardane); not a typo. yojyā is singular but applies to each plant named.
lines_deva: शणपुष्पी च बिम्बी च च्छर्दने हैमवत्यपि
lines_iast: śaṇapuṣpī ca bimbī ca cchardane haimavatyapi

hindi: जो ग्यारह शेष रहीं, उन्हें विरेचन में प्रयोग करना चाहिए। इस प्रकार नाम और कर्म से मूलिनी बता दी गईं; अब फलिनी सुनो।
english: The eleven that remain are to be used in purgation (virecana). Thus the root-drugs have been described by name and action; now hear the fruit-drugs.
notes: 16 root-drugs minus the 5 assigned in 79 (śaṇapuṣpī, bimbī, haimavatī for emesis; śvetā, jyotiṣmatī for head-evacuation) = 11.

hindi: शङ्खिनी, फिर विडङ्ग, त्रपुष और मदन; धामार्गव, फिर इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत और कृतवेधन; तथा क्लीतक, जो आनूप और स्थलज भेद से दो प्रकार का कहा गया है,
english: Śaṅkhinī, then viḍaṅga, trapuṣa and madana; dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta and kṛtavedhana; and klītaka, declared to be of two kinds, marsh-grown and land-grown,

text_flags.why: dvididha is not a word; dvi-vidha "of two kinds" fits sense and matches caturvidhaḥ in 86b.

notes: Line b recurs as 83b; this is not a duplication error: here it is part of the list of the 19 fruit-drugs, and at 83b it begins the list of their uses (83b + 84a = eight emetics). trapuṣam: the usual spelling is trapusa (dental s); trapuṣa is a known variant, so not flagged as an error. Identifications: viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes, Hindi वायविडंग (standard); trapusa = Cucumis sativus, cucumber, Hindi खीरा (standard); madana = Catunaregam spinosa (Randia dumetorum), Hindi मैनफल (standard); ikṣvāku = bitter Lagenaria siceraria, Hindi कड़वी तुम्बी (standard); dhāmārgava = a Luffa species, Hindi तोरई type (probable); jīmūta = Luffa echinata, Hindi देवदाली (probable); kṛtavedhana = bitter Luffa acutangula, कोशातकी (probable); klītaka = liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra, Hindi मुलेठी (probable; it is a root, which commentators discuss); śaṅkhinī = disputed.
lines_deva: आनूपं स्थलजं चैव क्लीतकं द्विदिधं स्मृतम्
lines_iast: ānūpaṃ sthalajaṃ caiva klītakaṃ dvididhaṃ smṛtam

hindi: प्रकीर्या, उदकीर्या, प्रत्यक्पुष्पा तथा अभया, अन्तःकोटरपुष्पी और हस्तिपर्णी का शरद् ऋतु का फल,
english: prakīryā and udakīryā, pratyakpuṣpā and likewise abhayā, antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī, and the autumn-gathered fruit of hastiparṇī,
notes: śāradam ("autumnal") is taken with an understood phalam: the fruit of hastiparṇī gathered in autumn. Identifications: pratyakpuṣpā = Achyranthes aspera, Hindi अपामार्ग, चिरचिटा (standard); abhayā = Terminalia chebula, Hindi हरड़ (standard); prakīryā = Caesalpinia bonduc or a karañja, Hindi पूतिकरंज (probable); udakīryā = Pongamia pinnata, Hindi करंज (probable); antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī = disputed (nīlinī and others proposed); hastiparṇī = disputed.

hindi: कम्पिल्लक और आरग्वध का फल, और कुटज का भी। धामार्गव, फिर इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत, कृतवेधन,
english: the fruit of kampillaka and of āragvadha, and that of kuṭaja. Dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana,
notes: GROUPING: line a ends the list of fruit-drugs; line b repeats 81b but starts a new sentence (the drugs for emesis and āsthāpana) that runs into 84a. The sense-grouping would be 83a with the list, and 83b + 84 together. Count of the fruit list (81a, 81b, 81c, 82, 83a): śaṅkhinī, viḍaṅga, trapuṣa, madana, dhāmārgava, ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana, klītaka of two kinds (2), prakīryā, udakīryā, pratyakpuṣpā, abhayā, antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī, hastiparṇī, kampillaka, āragvadha, kuṭaja = 19. Identifications: kampillaka = Mallotus philippensis, Hindi कमीला (standard); āragvadha = Cassia fistula, Hindi अमलतास (standard); kuṭaja = Holarrhena pubescens (H. antidysenterica), Hindi कुड़ा (standard).

hindi: मदन, कुटज, त्रपुष और हस्तिपर्णिनी — इन सबको वमन में और आस्थापन बस्तियों में प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: madana, kuṭaja, trapuṣa and hastiparṇinī: these are to be used in emesis (vamana) and in decoction enemas (āsthāpana).
notes: etāni covers the eight drugs of 83b and 84a. hastiparṇinī is taken as the same plant as hastiparṇī of 82b.

hindi: प्रत्यक्पुष्पा नाक के मार्ग से प्रच्छर्दन में विहित है। जो दस शेष हैं, वे विरेचन में बताए गए हैं।
english: Pratyakpuṣpā is prescribed for evacuation through the nose. The ten that remain are stated for purgation (virecana).
notes: nastaḥ pracchardana: expelling (doṣas) through the nose, i.e. errhine therapy. Count: 19 fruit-drugs minus 8 for emesis and āsthāpana (83b, 84a) minus 1 for nasal use (85a) = 10, as the text says.

hindi: उन्नीस फल नाम और कर्म से बताए गए। घी, तेल, वसा और मज्जा — स्नेह चार प्रकार का बताया गया है,
english: The nineteen fruits have been described by name and action. Ghee, oil, muscle fat and marrow: fat (sneha) is taught as fourfold,
notes: ekonaviṃśati = eka-ūna-viṃśati "twenty less one" = nineteen. vasā = fat of muscle tissue; majjā = bone marrow (in Sanskrit majjan/majjā; gender varies).

hindi: जो पान, अभ्यङ्ग, बस्ति और नस्य के लिए प्रयोग के अनुसार काम आता है। ये स्नेहन करने वाले, जीवन देने वाले, वर्ण के लिए हितकर तथा बल और शरीर की पुष्टि बढ़ाने वाले हैं।
english: for drinking, massage, enema and nasal medication, according to application. They are oleating, vitalising, good for the complexion, and increase strength and bodily bulk.
notes: yogataḥ may mean "according to the (proper) application" or "in combination (with other drugs)".

hindi: ये स्नेह वात, पित्त और कफ को दूर करने वाले बताए गए हैं। सौवर्चल, सैन्धव, विड और औद्भिद भी,
english: These fats are prescribed as removers of Vāta, Pitta and Kapha. Sauvarcala, saindhava (rock salt), viḍa and audbhida as well,
notes: The salt list continues into 89a. Identifications: saindhava = rock salt, Hindi सेंधा नमक (standard); sauvarcala = black salt, Hindi काला नमक or सौंचल (standard); viḍa = a manufactured salt, Hindi बिड़ नमक (standard); audbhida = salt that rises from the soil, efflorescent earth salt (probable).

hindi: ये समुद्री लवण के साथ पाँच लवण हैं। ये स्निग्ध, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण और अग्नि को सबसे अधिक दीप्त करने वाले हैं।
english: together with sea salt (sāmudra), these are the five salts. They are unctuous, hot, sharp and the most kindling of the digestive fire.

text_flags.why: transposed aspirate: the word is snigdha "unctuous" (as in 100a snigdhaṃ, 107a snigdhaṃ).

hindi: ये लेप के लिए, स्नेहन और स्वेदन की विधि में, अधोभाग और ऊर्ध्वभाग शोधन में, निरूह में और अनुवासन में प्रयोग किए जाते हैं;
english: They are used for plasters, likewise in the procedures of oleation and sudation, in downward and upward evacuation, in decoction enemas (nirūha) and in unctuous enema (anuvāsana),
notes: adhobhāga and ūrdhvabhāga: evacuation downward (purgation) and upward (emesis). The list of uses continues in 91–92.

hindi: अभ्यङ्ग में, भोजन के लिए, सिर के विरेचन में, शस्त्रकर्म में, वर्ति के लिए, तथा अञ्जन और उत्सादन में;
english: in massage, for food, in evacuation of the head, in surgical operations, for suppositories (varti), and in collyria and unctions,

text_flags.why: cirecana is not a word; śirasaḥ virecana "evacuation of the head" is the parallel of śīrṣavirecane in 79b; c/v confusion.

notes: utsādana: rubbing the body with a paste or powder.

hindi: और अजीर्ण, आनाह, वात रोग, गुल्म, शूल तथा उदर रोग में। लवण बता दिए गए; अब आगे मुझसे आठ मूत्रों को जानो,
english: and in indigestion and distension (ānāha), in Vāta disorder, in gulma (abdominal lump), colic and udara (abdominal enlargement). The salts have been described; next learn from me the eight urines,
notes: vāte: "in (disorders of) Vāta"; it could also be taken narrowly as flatulence. ānāha = distension with retention of faeces and wind.

hindi: जो प्रमुख हैं और सब आत्रेय के उपदेश में बताए गए हैं: भेड़ का मूत्र, बकरी का मूत्र, गाय का मूत्र और जो भैंस का है,
english: the principal ones, all of which are taught in the teaching of Ātreya: sheep urine, goat urine, cow urine, and that of the buffalo,
notes: mukhyāni continues the object of nibodha in 92b (acc.); yāni ... diṣṭāni is a relative clause.

hindi: हाथी का मूत्र, तथा ऊँट, घोड़े और गधे का मूत्र। मूत्र उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, अरूक्ष, कटु और लवण रस से युक्त होता है।
english: elephant urine, and that of the camel, the horse and the donkey. (Urine is) hot, sharp, not dry, pungent and accompanied by salt taste.
notes: atho'rūkṣam as printed with avagraha = atho arūkṣam "and not dry". Without the avagraha it would read atho rūkṣam "and dry"; the two readings give opposite properties, and editions and commentators differ. Kept as printed. The subject of line b (mūtram, urine in general) is understood.

hindi: मूत्र उत्सादन में प्रयुक्त होता है, लेपों में प्रयुक्त होता है, आस्थापन में प्रयुक्त होता है और विरेचन में भी प्रयुक्त होता है;
english: Urine is used in unction, used in plasters, used in decoction enema (āsthāpana), and used also in purgation,
notes: yuktam can mean "used" or "suitable"; rendered "used".

hindi: स्वेदों में भी वह प्रयुक्त होता है, तथा आनाह में, अगदों में, उदर रोगों में, अर्श में, और गुल्म, कुष्ठ तथा किलास के रोगियों में;
english: it is used also in sudations, in distension and in antidotes, in abdominal enlargements (udara) and in piles, and for those suffering from gulma, skin disease (kuṣṭha) and kilāsa (white patches of skin, leucoderma);
notes: kilāsa: a white skin disease, usually equated with leucoderma or vitiligo (probable). kuṣṭha covers skin diseases broadly, including but not limited to leprosy. ānāha in the context of a list of procedures could also mean a kind of sudation, but the plain sense "distension" is kept.

hindi: वह उपनाहों में और परिषेक में भी प्रयुक्त होता है। उसे अग्निदीपक, विषनाशक और कृमिनाशक बताया जाता है।
english: it is used in poultices (upanāha) and likewise in affusion (pariṣeka). It is taught to be kindling of the digestive fire, destroying poison and destroying worms.
notes: pariṣeka: pouring liquid over the body or a part.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. m. gen. pl. upa-√sṛj

words.gloss: would move in the right direction

hindi: पाण्डुरोग से पीड़ित लोगों के लिए इसे उत्तम सुख देने वाला कहा गया है। पिया हुआ मूत्र कफ को शान्त करता है और वायु का अनुलोमन करता है,
english: and it is said to be the best relief for those afflicted with pāṇḍu disease (pallor, anaemia). When drunk it pacifies Kapha (śleṣman) and moves wind (māruta, Vāta) in its proper direction,

text_flags.why: ppp. of upa-√sṛj is upasṛṣṭa with retroflex ṭ; dental t is a typing slip.

notes: pāṇḍu roga: a disease of pallor, usually equated with anaemia (standard). anulomayet: makes Vāta move downward, in its natural direction.

hindi: और पित्त को नीचे के मार्ग से निकालता है। इस प्रकार इसका गुण-संग्रह मैंने सामान्य रूप से कहा; अब अलग-अलग कहा जाएगा।
english: and draws Pitta out downwards. Thus the summary of its properties has been told by me in general terms; it will now be described separately.
notes: asmin: "in this (urine)". pravakṣyate is formally a future middle, used here in a passive sense.

hindi: भेड़ का मूत्र तिक्त रस से युक्त, स्निग्ध और पित्त का विरोधी न होने वाला है। बकरी का मूत्र कषाय और मधुर, पथ्य है और दोषों को नष्ट करता है।
english: Sheep urine is slightly bitter, unctuous and not hostile to Pitta. Goat urine is astringent and sweet, wholesome, and destroys the doṣas.
notes: satikta: "with bitterness", i.e. having a bitter taste in addition (often rendered "slightly bitter"). pittāvirodhi: literally "not hostile to Pitta", i.e. does not provoke it.
lines_deva: अविमूत्रं सतिक्तं स्यात् स्निग्धं पित्ताविरोधि च
lines_iast: avimūtraṃ satiktaṃ syāt snigdhaṃ pittāvirodhi ca

hindi: गाय का मूत्र कुछ मधुर, कुछ दोषनाशक, कृमि और कुष्ठ को दूर करने वाला है। पिया हुआ यह खुजली को शान्त करता है और दोषज उदर रोग में भली-भाँति हितकर है।
english: Cow urine has some sweetness, is somewhat doṣa-destroying, and dispels worms and skin disease (kuṣṭha). When drunk it relieves itching and is properly beneficial in udara (abdominal enlargement) caused by the doṣas.
notes: kiṃcit may qualify samadhuram ("slightly sweet") or doṣaghnam ("somewhat doṣa-destroying"); both readings are possible. samyak may go with pītam ("when properly drunk") or with hitam. doṣodara is taken as udara arising from the doṣas.
lines_deva: कण्डूं च शमयेत् पीतं सम्यग्दोषोदरे हितम्
lines_iast: kaṇḍūṃ ca śamayet pītaṃ samyagdoṣodare hitam

words.gram: possessive -in on dvandva krimi-kuṣṭha, m. gen. pl.

hindi: भैंस का मूत्र अर्श, शोथ और उदर रोग को नष्ट करने वाला, क्षार से युक्त और सर है। हाथी का मूत्र लवण है और कृमि तथा कुष्ठ के रोगियों के लिए हितकर है।
english: Buffalo urine destroys piles, swelling (śopha) and udara, is alkaline and laxative (sara). Elephant urine is salty and beneficial for those suffering from worms and skin disease.
notes: krimi-kuṣṭhinām: "for those having worms and kuṣṭha" (krimi- as first member with kuṣṭhin).
lines_deva: हास्तिकं लवणं मूत्रं हितं तु क्रिमिकुष्ठिनाम्
lines_iast: hāstikaṃ lavaṇaṃ mūtraṃ hitaṃ tu krimikuṣṭhinām

hindi: वह मल-मूत्र के रुकने, विष, कफ के रोगों और अर्श में प्रशस्त है। ऊँट का मूत्र तिक्त रस से युक्त, श्वास, कास और अर्श को नष्ट करने वाला कहा जाता है।
english: It (elephant urine) is recommended for obstruction of faeces and urine, poison, Kapha disorders and piles. Camel urine is said to be slightly bitter and to destroy dyspnoea (śvāsa), cough and piles.
notes: Line a most naturally continues the elephant urine of 102b. The compound is read as baddha-viṇmūtra (retention of faeces and urine), viṣa, śleṣmāmaya (Kapha disorders), arśas; other groupings are possible. śvāsa: difficult breathing, often equated with asthma (probable).

hindi: घोड़ों का मूत्र तिक्त और कटु है तथा कुष्ठ, व्रण और विष को दूर करता है। गधे का मूत्र अपस्मार, उन्माद और ग्रह-बाधा को नष्ट करने वाला है।
english: That of horses is bitter and pungent and removes skin disease, wounds and poison. Donkey urine destroys epilepsy (apasmāra), insanity (unmāda) and seizure by spirits (graha).
notes: vājinām: genitive plural, with mūtram understood. apasmāra = epilepsy (standard); unmāda = insanity, psychosis (standard); graha = possession or seizure by supernatural beings, as the text conceives it.

hindi: इस प्रकार यहाँ मूत्र उनके सामर्थ्य और प्रयोग के अनुसार बताए गए। अब दूध बताए जाएँगे, और इनका कर्म तथा जो इनके गुण हैं।
english: Thus the urines have been described here according to their efficacy and application. Next the milks will be described, with their action and their properties.
notes: yathāsāmarthyayogataḥ could also mean "according to their efficacy in combination (with other drugs)".
lines_deva: अतः क्षीराणि वक्ष्यन्ते कर्म चैषां गुणाश्च ये
lines_iast: ataḥ kṣīrāṇi vakṣyante karma caiṣāṃ guṇāśca ye

hindi: भेड़ का दूध, बकरी का दूध, गाय का दूध और जो भैंस का है, फिर ऊँटनियों का, हथिनियों का, घोड़ी का और स्त्री का दूध।
english: Sheep milk, goat milk, cow milk and that of the buffalo; then that of she-camels, of she-elephants, of the mare and likewise of woman.
notes: Eight milks, as stated in 75b.

hindi: दूध प्रायः मधुर, स्निग्ध, शीत और स्तन्य बढ़ाने वाला माना गया है; यह तृप्त करने वाला, बृंहण, वृष्य, मेधा के लिए हितकर, बलकारक और मन को स्फूर्ति देने वाला है,
english: Milk is generally held to be sweet, unctuous, cold and promoting of breast milk; it is nourishing, bulk-promoting (bṛṃhaṇa), aphrodisiac, good for the intellect, strengthening and invigorating to the mind,
notes: stanyam: taken as "promoting breast milk" (galactagogue); it could also be read as "(like) breast milk". manaskara: literally "mind-making", i.e. invigorating or cheering the mind.
lines_deva: प्रायशो मधुरं स्निग्धं शीतं स्तन्यं पयो मतम्
प्रीणनं बृंहणं वृष्यं मेध्यं बल्यं मनस्करम्
lines_iast: prāyaśo madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ śītaṃ stanyaṃ payo matam
prīṇanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ medhyaṃ balyaṃ manaskaram

hindi: जीवनीय, थकान दूर करने वाला, श्वास और कास को मिटाने वाला है; यह रक्तपित्त को नष्ट करता है और आहत को जोड़ने वाला है,
english: vitalising, removing fatigue, removing dyspnoea and cough; it destroys śoṇitapitta (bleeding disorder) and is a uniter of what is injured,
notes: śoṇitapitta = raktapitta, a bleeding disorder (haemorrhage from various orifices) (standard). vihatasya: of an injured or broken (part); sandhāna = joining, healing. The sentence continues into the next unit.
lines_deva: हन्ति शोणितपित्तं च सन्धानं विहतस्य च
lines_iast: hanti śoṇitapittaṃ ca sandhānaṃ vihatasya ca
